hypothesis_text: When retail trader positioning reaches extreme long or short crowding (captured by |long_short_ratio_zscore_4h| > 1.6), order book liquidity and speculative flow become highly asymmetric. Subsequent aggressive order flow leaning against the crowded retail cohort (taker_buy_ratio_1h gate_opposite_side) triggers an inventory unwind, driving systematic price mean reversion (predicted_sign = -1) over 1h to 12h horizon bands across Layer-1 altcoins.
narrative: Retail accounts on perpetual exchanges exhibit persistent herd behavior, piling into directional momentum late in price moves and creating severe positioning skew measured by the 4-hour account long/short ratio z-score (|long_short_ratio_zscore_4h| > 1.6). When retail is heavily crowded long (z > 1.6), market makers and informed institutional traders hold the opposite (short) inventory and charge funding. Once aggressive taker order flow turns against the retail crowd (gate_opposite_side on taker_buy_ratio_1h, or taker selling against retail longs), market makers rapidly lower bids to protect inventory, triggering retail stop-loss cascades and forced margin liquidations. Conversely, when retail is crowded short (z < -1.6), aggressive buying creates a short squeeze that forces panic short covering. In both tails, the mechanical requirement for the crowded side to exit illiquid positions under adverse selection forces mean-reverting price action over the subsequent 1h to 12h horizons.
research_rationale: Anchor statistics and empirical distribution: On the 15m scan panel across the l1_alt universe (288,855 rows, 430 days, June 2024 - August 2025), long_short_ratio_zscore_4h exhibits mean 0.009, std 1.255, with 10th and 90th percentiles at -1.60 and +1.63. The condition |long_short_ratio_zscore_4h| > 1.6 isolates the outer ~20.5% tail (59,196 matched rows, 27,134 episodes, 430 active days, 430 independent events), perfectly balanced between positive (30,272) and negative (28,924) crowding regimes. Autocorrelation drops to near zero at 4h (-0.03) and 24h (-0.004), demonstrating that 4h sentiment shocks represent genuine, episodic positioning imbalances rather than sticky multi-week regimes. Composition design and gene priors: We commit four targeted composition terms following gene_knowledge.priors (SENTIMENT anchor): 1. gate_opposite_side on taker_buy_ratio_1h: Implements the trigger role from gene priors (n=123, confidence sufficient, shrink_weight 0.86), where aggressive taker flow leaning against retail crowd positioning starts the unwind. On candidate bars, gate_opposite_side matches 6,589 rows across 429 days (2,430 projected T1 event observations at 60m, comfortably exceeding the 250 event floor). 2. gate_high on taker_buy_ratio_1h (4,524 rows, 1,707 event obs) and 3. gate_low on taker_buy_ratio_1h (5,315 rows, 1,904 event obs): Committed as essential controls for the side-tied gate to satisfy server requirements and prevent sign confounding. 4. gate_tail on trend_sma_ratio_24h: Implements the stretch role from gene priors (n=48, confidence sufficient, shrink_weight 0.706), isolating episodes where price has stretched relative to its 24h trend (9,907 rows, 333 scored days, 2,456 event obs), separating crowd exhaustion from trend continuation. Cemetery analysis response: In the cemetery ledger for long_short_ratio_zscore_4h (2,476 trials), the dominant kill code was T0.04-IC-STAT (1,757 trials) and T1.10-ICIR (265 trials) occurring primarily on raw single-gene dense formulas (survival rate 0.0%) and long horizons (4h-1d survival rate 0.0%). In contrast, 30m-2h horizons and gated structures exhibited the highest survival rates (30m survival 10.9%, 1h survival 5.0%, min/gate_high survival 4-11%). By combining a locked tail condition with event gates (taker flow trigger and trend stretch), we restrict trading to high-conviction episodic liquidity cascades, substantially increasing the expected information coefficient while minimizing continuous turnover costs.
